rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Introduces a material territory-size parameter that was absent from the prior disclosure.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Addition of a sentence limiting enforceability of extra-contractual representations changes the contractual scope of the integration clause.

2 atomic changes. The FPR annual outlet universe for affiliate-owned restaurants increased from 8 to 9, a clear coverage/method change. The FPR annual outlet universe for franchisee-owned restaurants increased from 8 to 9, a clear coverage/method change.

4 atomic changes. The state coverage of projected openings changed from California and Texas to Hawaii. Projected number of signed-but-unopened franchise agreements changed from zero to one in the disclosed table.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 5 atomic changes. The mandatory $200/month Maintenance fee obligation was removed from the Digital Advertising Program description. Required participation in the Digital Advertising Program changed to an optional opportunity, removing a mandatory obligation.

5 atomic changes. Good Standing metric changed from actual monthly Advertising Value to contracted monthly Advertising Value, altering how the condition is measured. Good Standing condition threshold increased from $18,000 to $20,000 per month, a material increase in the franchisee's required advertising value.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Material increase in the required monthly advertising value as a condition for franchisor approval of transfer, increasing franchisee burden. Clear change in the integration clause scope, altering which representations are potentially enforceable.

5 atomic changes. Removal of licensed business data from FPR materially narrows the outlet population disclosed. Changing the reporting unit from per-magazine to per-franchised-business fundamentally alters the meaning of all performance statistics.
1 atomic change. Restated number of franchised outlets opened in 2020 increased from 24 to 25; a disclosure correction.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. The franchise definition is expanded from general business brokerage to explicitly require operation of a Sunbelt Business Brokers business serving main street and middle market businesses. The new version introduces an explicit, enumerated list of securities laws with which the franchisee must comply, substantively expanding the disclosed compliance obligation.
1 atomic change. Franchisor management structure changed from no officers or Directors to a named President.

2 atomic changes. Removal of the franchisor's discretion to require pre-payment of ongoing monthly fees in connection with the initial fee; a material change in potential fee obligations. New explicit disclosure that the franchisor does not finance the initial franchise fee; a clear disclosure-method change.

5 atomic changes. The due date for convention/seminar fees changed from 'as incurred' to at registration. The due date for the audit fee changed from 'as incurred' to within 30 days of the audit, a clear timing change.

1 atomic change. Changes the disclosed refundability of all non-franchise-fee costs from blanket non-refundable to conditionally refundable at supplier discretion, a material change in financial risk.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 6 atomic changes. Deadline shortened from 90 to 60 days, a clear timing and obligation change. Removal of disclosed limitation on franchisor's modification of Operations Manuals.

2 atomic changes. Removal of a contractual obligation on the franchisee to focus marketing efforts within the Territory. Addition of explicit worldwide scope to franchisor's reserved right to sell services under other marks expands franchisor's competitive latitude.
1 atomic change. New disclosure statement added about current plans regarding similar-business trademark use; a disclosure-method change.
1 atomic change. Expands confidentiality obligation from manuals to all communicated information, a clear operational/contract change.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. Removal of an explicit franchisee obligation to form a business entity is a material contractual change. The guaranty scope changed from 20%+ owners (and spouses) to all owners, a material expansion of the personal guaranty obligation.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 3 atomic changes. The explicit franchisor reservation to change authorized services was removed. The authorized service scope was redefined from training-consistent business brokerage to representation in privately held business sales and franchise opportunity transactions.
1 atomic change. Addition of a new disclosure item (unaudited interim financial statements) that provides additional financial information to prospective franchisees.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Estimated annual ongoing technical support cost increased from $700 to $1,000.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The manager qualification for aggregating 60% working time across multiple locations changed from 'trained' to 'named', a clear operational condition change.

2 atomic changes. A new alternative performance figure was introduced, adding a distinct disclosed calculation. The reported average gross revenue figure changed and the reporting year changed from 2015 to 2016.
1 atomic change. Moving the named distribution center changes the geographic reference point for the free delivery zone, which is a clear operational change to the Delivery Fee row.
1 atomic change. Removal of a stated employee personal vehicle requirement for optional delivery; limited operational change.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The addition of electronic access as an option for providing the Operations Manual changes the method of a required assistance without altering fees or obligations.
1 atomic change. Removal of a registered trademark from the licensed mark list reduces the scope of marks available to franchisees.
1 atomic change. Clear operational change adding a new eligibility condition to the expansion-program discount.
5 atomic changes. A 20% annual Base Fee increase cap was introduced, along with a right to increase within that cap. A contractual monthly maximum Base Fee was introduced.
1 atomic change. Structural change in the discount formula from percentage to flat amount.
1 atomic change. A new pending lawsuit against parents/affiliates is disclosed in the 2025 Item 3 and was absent from the complete 2024 Item 3.
9 atomic changes. Removal of the only refund exception for the Application Fee changes the refundability condition. Removal of a disclosed mandatory-looking fee and associated service.
19 atomic changes. Per-additional-attendee conference fee increased by $250. Per-attendee conference fee increased by $200.

16 atomic changes. Disclosed Additional Funds estimate for conversion increased from $142,432-$204,261 to $146,873-$210,557. Disclosed Additional Funds for 3 Month Initial Period estimate increased from $148,824-$210,653 to $153,474-$217,158.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. The required Approved Supplier purchase category for health and safety expanded from 'items' to 'services' and now explicitly includes sanitation and cleanliness. New disclosure that commissions can sometimes be as high as 10% of net or gross sales.
1 atomic change. The typical procurement services fee as a percentage of FF&E cost increased from 10%-15% to 11%-17%, raising a conditional fee.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 14 atomic changes. Extension of the construction start deadline by six months, easing franchisee timing burden. Extension of the construction completion deadline by six months, reducing franchisee time pressure.
1 atomic change. Adds a new trigger (notice of termination) under which the Protected Territory may be impacted, expanding the franchisor's rights to modify territory.
1 atomic change. Addition of a new disclosure describing the franchisor's exclusive license to use and sublicense the marks is a material content change.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on What the Franchisee May Sell
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. New grant of sole discretion to franchisor to establish a discount program shifts control toward franchisor. New mandatory participation obligation in a discount rate program materially changes franchisee obligations.
3 atomic changes. Disclosure-method change to the eligible population threshold. Added a new performance disclosure table for Qualified Chain Facilities.

2 atomic changes. Disclosed projection of signed-but-not-opened franchise agreements increased from 159 to 166. Disclosed projection of new franchised outlets in the next fiscal year increased from 28 to 45.
1 atomic change. The franchisor removed the interim unaudited condensed financial statements from Exhibit D, changing the scope of financial disclosures in Item 21.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Operational count of Branded Menu Program locations changed from 81 to 75, reflecting a disclosed change in the size of that program.
1 atomic change. New disclosure caveat added to Item 7 Note 23; no dollar amounts or fee terms changed, but the estimate's scope is clarified.

6 atomic changes. Prior-year reported franchised Arthur Treacher's outlet count for fiscal 2024 was revised from 41 to 48. Prior-year reported franchised BMP outlet count for fiscal 2024 was revised from 90 to 81.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Addition of a new affiliate that offers franchises in Brazil is a clear change in the franchisor's affiliate network and franchise-offering scope.

9 atomic changes. Introduces a new conditional fee for alternative design review requests. Removal of a conditional $50,000 application-fee discount materially increases potential initial fees for eligible applicants.
15 atomic changes. The daily training fee increased by $75 per trainer. A new optional Central Sales Services Program with multiple service tiers and fee ranges was introduced.

8 atomic changes. A new fee row for alternative design services review was introduced with an estimated range of $0 to $30,000. Both bounds of the architecture and design estimate increased, with the upper bound rising from $866,143 to $1,200,000.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Introduces a new condition under which the franchisor can require franchisee participation in Central Services Agreement services as mandatory. Introduces an exception to the prior statement that no officers owned supplier interests, disclosing a potential conflict of interest.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 14 atomic changes. The designated PMS/POS vendor's current per-room monthly charge disclosed in Item 11 decreased from $6.65 to $3.90. New sentence obligates franchisee to pay the franchisor's then-current fees for requested additional pre-opening assistance, a conditional fee obligation absent from old Item 11.

3 atomic changes. Expansion of the Confidential Information definition from Hyatt Place Hotels to all Brand Hotels materially increases the franchisee's confidentiality obligations. Expansion of the Innovation assignment obligation from Hyatt Place Hotel to all Brand Hotels materially broadens the franchisee's obligation to assign innovations.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 8 atomic changes. Introduces a data-access control restricting who may access revenue management systems and data. Introduces a new franchisor discretion to impose remedial requirements at franchisee expense as an alternative to revocation.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 9 atomic changes. Fundamentally restructures the ancillary services contracts from separate agreements to a single Central Services Agreement with multiple program schedules. Replaces the fixed 2-year no-termination period for a required marketing agreement with a franchisor-specified 'certain date' condition, expanding franchisor discretion over schedule termination timing.
1 atomic change. Clear addition of a new disclosure element (Form 8-K exhibit) to Item 21.

2 atomic changes. The contract attached as Exhibit I was replaced with a different agreement, altering the franchise relationship documents. The Field Marketing Program Opt-In Agreement was removed from the list of attached agreements.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 2 atomic changes. Material change in contract rights, introducing a franchisee termination right where none existed. Clear operational timing change in a renewal condition.

4 atomic changes. New provision gives franchisor the right to collect and spend required local advertising expenditures. New provision caps any IT Fee increase to actual cost increases plus up to 10% overhead, limiting franchisor discretion.
5 atomic changes. The disclosed additional funds estimate for the first three months rose materially. Material increase in the disclosed construction cost range for the same 6,000 sq ft center.

rows.itemTitle: Restrictions on Sources of Products and Services
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. A new $500 per month digital marketing spend floor is introduced, increasing the fixed local advertising obligation. The percentage-of-Gross-Sales alternative increased from 2% to 3.0%, a material increase in the required local advertising spend when the percentage applies.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 11 atomic changes. A new contractual cap on IT Fee increases was introduced, limiting the franchisor's ability to raise the fee. The percentage-of-Gross-Sales local advertising requirement increased from 2.0% to 3.0%.

3 atomic changes. The new item removes a risk disclosure about unregistered principal trademarks, changing the disclosed risk profile. A principal trademark changed from pending application to federal registration, a clear legal status change.

rows.itemTitle: Obligation to Participate in the Actual Operation of the Franchise Business
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. Clear operational timing change: the replacement Director now may complete training at the next scheduled applicable training as an alternative to the 90-day deadline.

11 atomic changes. The daily member rate disclosure changed from a single Glenner rate to a state/payor schedule. The sample center changed from a franchised unit to a corporate-owned Perry Hall unit, altering the basis of the performance representation.
7 atomic changes. Clear increase in the reported number of franchised outlets at the end of the latest year, from 7 to 8. Material decrease in the number of signed agreements in Florida, from 5 to 2.

rows.itemTitle: The Franchisor and Any Parents, Predecessors, and Affiliates
rows.summary: 4 atomic changes. Introduction of a conditional developer incentive program with material economic benefit to qualifying franchisees. New affiliate introduced as offering MGallery franchises in Mexico.

1 atomic change. The 2025 FDD removes the pending-litigation disclosure that the 2024 FDD included for a class action against the franchisor's parent and states affirmatively that no litigation is required to be disclosed, a material change in the Item 3 disclosed litigation-risk profile.
2 atomic changes. Introduces a conditional material reduction in the Initial Franchise Fee for qualifying hotels. Operational scope change in the services covered by the same fee amount.

2 atomic changes. Marketing Fund Fee rate changes from flat 1.5% to 1.5% or less if Developer Incentive qualification, a material fee change. Royalty rate changes from flat 5% to 5% or 3% conditional on Developer Incentive qualification, a material fee change.

7 atomic changes. Project management fee changed from fixed $6,000 to a $10,000-$50,000 range, increasing the minimum and giving the franchisor discretion over the amount. Initial franchise fee changed from fixed $75,000 to a $20,000-$75,000 range with a conditional Developer Incentive discount.
1 atomic change. New provision gives the franchisor discretion to require a comfort letter when the franchisee obtains third-party financing, adding a conditional obligation.

rows.itemTitle: Franchisor's Assistance, Advertising, Computer Systems, and Training
rows.summary: 21 atomic changes. AccorSecure annual fee increased from $270 to $325 per account. Introduces a conditional exception to the previously unconditional computer system fee obligations.

rows.itemTitle: Renewal, Termination, Transfer, and Dispute Resolution
rows.summary: 1 atomic change. The disclosed initial franchise term changed from a general 10-20 year range to a typical 20-year term with franchisor discretion for deviations and a 10-year Developer Incentive term, a material change to the core term of the franchise relationship.

2 atomic changes. The as-of date for the Exhibit G franchisee list changed from the disclosure document date to the last fiscal year end, a disclosure-method change. Exhibit H's inclusion window expanded to add franchisees ceasing business since the last fiscal year end, a disclosure-scope change.
1 atomic change. New disclosure of affiliate ownership of company-owned outlets is a clear disclosure-method change.
